channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: Jet fuel raised ₹1.37 a litre to ₹138.50, a fourth monthly rise; commercial LPG up ₹10 to ₹2,820
item.description:
Household LPG held at ₹942 per cylinder. Second straight monthly hike in commercial LPG as international benchmarks firm. Ongoing pass-through of high oil.

Why it matters: Dearer jet fuel squeezes airline margins and fares; commercial LPG adds to restaurant and small-business costs, while frozen household prices keep the subsidy burden on the state.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Iran says talks are under way on a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz; envoys meet Qatari and Pakistani mediators
item.description:
Tehran wants sanctions lifted, oil waivers restored and frozen funds released; another official called Qatar's ideas unacceptable. Iran's leader ordered an 'unrestricted response' to any attack. Diplomacy advancing but contested.

Why it matters: A quick reopening would sharply lower India's oil, LNG and freight costs; failure raises the risk of US strikes after the 3 November vote.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance +1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: low · horizon: weeks

item.title: Foreign investors pulled ₹52,100 crore from Indian equities in October; 2026 outflows reach ₹3.12 lakh crore
item.description:
Up from ₹48,056 crore reported mid-month despite late-month buying. Crude near $114, US yields and the pull of AI stocks elsewhere drove selling. Foreign funds also sold debt. Ongoing.

Why it matters: Persistent foreign selling weighs on large caps and the rupee, leaving domestic funds to absorb supply.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows −2, Rupee −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months

item.title: Rupee ends October with its best month since February, up about 0.6–1%
item.description:
RBI steps included a special oil-dollar window and moving oil-related dollar buying off the spot market, while tight liquidity made shorting the rupee costly. Reversing earlier weakness.

Why it matters: A steadier rupee eases imported inflation and reassures foreign investors, but relies on RBI support as reserves fall.

Market gauges: Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: India's record crude imports point to strong refinery runs; Russian oil buying to stay flexible
item.description:
Refiners keep buying heavily despite prices near $118, shifting between Gulf and Russian grades on price. Continues last week's sourcing shift.

Why it matters: High refinery runs support fuel exports and refining margins, but record volumes at high prices swell the import bill.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: US Navy could escort ships through Hormuz with an international coalition, Treasury Secretary says
item.description:
Comes as October set a record for ship attacks and Iran claims tankers on unauthorised routes caught fire. New proposal.

Why it matters: Escorts could restore some tanker traffic and ease freight and insurance costs for India, but risk direct clashes.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance +1

Confidence: low · horizon: weeks

item.title: India and Turkey propose ideas to resume Black Sea grain shipments, US says at G20
item.description:
Black Sea attacks have made it deadlier than Hormuz; Türkiye submitted proposals to the US and others call for a truce. Builds on last week's corridor proposal.

Why it matters: Restored Black Sea flows would ease world grain and edible oil prices, helping India's food inflation.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: low · horizon: months

item.title: At G20, India flags Hormuz ship attacks and urges shielding energy markets from sanctions and chokepoints
item.description:
The external affairs minister said the Global South bears the burden and Indian seafarers face risks. Follows attacks on ships with Indian crews. Diplomatic push.

Why it matters: Signals India's push for supply security; limited direct market effect but supports diplomacy that could lower energy risk.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: low · horizon: months
